evidence: Quint. 1.5.42: in quibus nōs singulārem ac plūrālem habēmus
terms.comment: numerus singulāris, the singular number; numerī singulāris, in the singular (Traupman 238); adverb singulāriter, in the singular (Quint. 1.5.16; Traupman 248). Latin, Quintilian notes, has singular and plural where Greek also has a dual.

phrases.latin: nōn aliō vitiōsa sunt, quam quod plūrālia singulāriter et singulāria plūrāliter efferuntur
phrases.english: they are wrong only in this, that plurals are spoken in the singular and singulars in the plural

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 221, p. 238, p. 248.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
